story.head: DeBrincat’s favorite opponent
paras: The Red Wings (8-11-3) lost 4-1 to Boston on Nov 18, while the Blue Jackets (8-12-0) beat Chicago 4-2 on Nov 19. Going in, the Red Wings are seventh in the Atlantic (tied for 26th in the NHL) and the Blue Jackets seventh in the Metropolitan (tied for 28th).

The Red Wings have played better than their record (.432) says: their chances are worth about .542, and their finishing has held them back. So have the Blue Jackets (.400 on chances worth .492), where their finishing has held them back.
This season, the Red Wings have been outscored 66-56, but only 41-37 at 5-on-5. On special teams, opponents have outscored them 20-11.

The Red Wings block more shots than almost anyone (2nd) and take away shots from the point (4th lowest), but ice the puck a lot (30th). The Blue Jackets forecheck as hard as almost anyone (3rd) and do a lot of their shooting from distance (3rd lowest). They also get their defensemen shooting (3rd), so their defensemen shoot a lot, and the Red Wings’ not so much. Columbus has scored 2.40 goals a game, the fewest in the league. The Wings’ power play (6th) could do real damage against the Blue Jackets’ penalty kill (23rd).

Lucas Raymond (9 G / 13 A / 22 P in 22 GP) leads the Red Wings in scoring. Alex DeBrincat (7 G / 9 A / 16 P in 22 GP) is next in line, with a point in nine straight games against Columbus. For the Blue Jackets, Kent Johnson (9 G / 12 A / 21 P in 20 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Zach Werenski (4 G / 14 A / 18 P in 20 GP) is next in line.

Cam Talbot (6-4-0 / .907 SV% in 10 GS) will likely start for Columbus. Detroit has two options in net: Daniil Tarasov (3-4-2 / .927 SV% in 8 GS) and John Gibson (4-7-1 / .862 SV% in 13 GS). They have split the last ten starts, and Tarasov got the last one on Nov 18. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
